text: Opening: Lexora is a browser-based workbench for compiler-design assignments. It runs real Flex and Bison specifications and provides a separate educational analysis of program input. Suggested presentation duration: 12–15 minutes. Implementation sources: README.md; frontend/src/App.jsx; backend/services/compiler.js; backend/services/inputAnalysis.js.

text: Local development topology. Vite serves port 3000 and proxies /api to Express on port 3001. The compiler runs in WSL Ubuntu on Windows or native Bash on Linux. The JavaScript educational analyzer runs in the Node backend. Browser localStorage is local to that browser origin. Sources: frontend/vite.config.js; frontend/src/App.jsx; backend/server.js; backend/services/wslRunner.js; backend/services/compiler.js.

text: Each compilation has two conceptual result paths. In the implementation analyzeInput runs before the native toolchain steps. They are separate computations, not concurrent processes. Invalid requests stop in validation before compiler orchestration. Temporary-directory cleanup runs in finally before the route returns JSON. Sources: frontend/src/App.jsx; backend/routes/compile.js; backend/middleware/validator.js; backend/services/compiler.js.

title: How Lex and Yacc become an executable

text: How Lex and Yacc become an executable
textPreview: How Lex and Yacc become an executable

text: Lex-only skips Bison. Yacc-only must provide its own yylex() and main().
textPreview: Lex-only skips Bison. Yacc-only must provide its own yylex() and main().

text: Actual combined-mode order: flex lex.l; bison -d parser.y; normalize references such as y.tab.h to parser.tab.h and regenerate Flex; gcc -o compiler lex.yy.c parser.tab.c -lfl -lm; ./compiler < input.txt. Bison defaults to LALR(1), while supporting other parser table types when requested. Sources: backend/services/compiler.js; https://westes.github.io/flex/manual/Introduction.html; https://www.gnu.org/s/bison/manual/bison.html; https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Overall-Options.html

text: The displayed educational TAC does not become the native executable.
textPreview: The displayed educational TAC does not become the native executable.

text: This distinction prevents a misleading claim that arbitrary user grammars automatically produce all educational outputs. analyzeInput reads inputCode with Lexora’s own tokenizer and recursive-descent parser. The educational TAC never feeds GCC. Native diagnostics remain authoritative for the user-supplied program. Sources: README.md; backend/services/inputAnalysis.js; backend/services/compiler.js.
The optimizer transforms TAC. Basic-block detection partitions the original TAC.
textPreview: The optimizer transforms TAC. Basic-block detection partitions the original TAC.

text: The implementation computes tokens and then parseAST(input), whose parser handles its own tokenization. This diagram shows the conceptual learning phases. Semantic analysis and TAC both use the AST. Basic blocks use original TAC. Sources: backend/services/inputAnalysis.js; tokenExtractor.js; astGenerator.js; semanticAnalyzer.js; tacGenerator.js; optimizer.js; basicBlocks.js.
Multiplication groups 3 and 4 before the addition to 2.
textPreview: Multiplication groups 3 and 4 before the addition to 2.

text: x is an integer variable declared in global scope.
textPreview: x is an integer variable declared in global scope.

text: Observed directly using analyzeInput("int x = 2 + 3 * 4;"). Nine tokens. AST root is Declaration, datatype int, variable x. Expression has addition at root and multiplication in the right branch. Symbol x has type int, kind variable, global scope, declared true and used false. This is educational analysis, not a claim that the calculator grammar accepts C declarations. Source: backend/services/inputAnalysis.js.
Constant folding evaluates arithmetic. Constant propagation substitutes known values.
textPreview: Constant folding evaluates arithmetic. Constant propagation substitutes known values.

text: This example has one basic block because it contains no branches.
textPreview: This example has one basic block because it contains no branches.

text: Actual output of analyzeInput("int x = 2 + 3 * 4;"). Original TAC: t1 = 3 * 4; t2 = 2 + t1; x = t2. Optimized TAC: t1 = 12; t2 = 14; x = 14. The optimizer retains three assignments in this example, so do not claim instruction-count reduction or measured speedup. Source: backend/services/optimizer.js and observed analyzer output.

Versions derive from package.json dependency ranges, not installed-version measurements. Frontend uses React 19 and Vite 8, superseding older architecture notes mentioning React 18. Avoid claiming exact toolchain versions unless measured on the demonstration machine. Sources: frontend/package.json; backend/package.json; backend/services/wslRunner.js; Dockerfile.

text: These limits describe actual implementation boundaries. This is a trusted local workbench. Native C actions execute with backend-user privileges. WSL, timeouts and per-job folders are not a security sandbox. Public untrusted submissions require real isolation. Sources: README.md; backend/services/wslRunner.js. Future work is proposed, not implemented.
